fields.Participants: Marketing Ops Mgr, VP Marketing, Vendor, DC
fields.Trigger: Gift card inventory reorder point or new design launch

Automation Opportunity: - Stock-level auto-monitored with reorder at threshold; sequential-number range auto-registered to ERP on vendor shipment
Controls: - CTL-391 (ensure controlled execution — Gift Card Issuance & Distribution (PA-54.1).)
- operational: Marketing Ops monthly stock-reconciliation sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unactivated-card-loss risk**: physical cards lost/stolen before activation are worthless (no liability until activation), but loss signals weak controls; mitigated by the sequential-number registry and the store-level stock-count reconciliation
- **Design-obsolescence risk**: a quarterly new-design launch leaves the prior design as dead stock; mitigated by the design-phase-out plan (sell-through the old before activating the new)
System Touchpoints: - Gift-card/stored-value module (links to VS-08 / W28 gift card liability, VS-29 / W296 service-item master) — the card-SKU and the activation registry
- Inventory (links to VS-05 / W6 cycle counting) — the physical-card stock tracking (distinct from the stored-value liability)
- DC distribution (links to VS-04 / W3) — card allocation to stores
Time Estimate: ~6 hours/month Marketing Ops + DC handling absorbed = **~70–90 hours/year**.

steps.activity: Marketing Ops Manager monitors physical gift card stock across 200 stores; reorder triggers at minimum threshold; coordinates with card vendor for production (security features, sequential numbering, BuildRight branding)
Vendor produces cards with embedded security (sequential numbering registered to ERP at activation); ships to DC for distribution; DC allocates to stores based on sell-through rate

fields.Trigger: Customer purchases gift card at POS

workflows.name: Gift Card Sale & Activation at POS

Automation Opportunity: - Activation and liability-posting fully automated in the POS flow; AMLA KYC auto-prompted at the threshold
Controls: - CTL-391 (ensure controlled execution — Gift Card Issuance & Distribution (PA-54.1).)
- operational: Store Manager daily-close review of gift-card activations
Pain Points / Risks: - **Activation-failure risk**: the customer pays but the card doesn't activate (system glitch), so the stored-value never loads and the customer loses their money; mitigated by the activation-confirmation receipt and the W2158 daily liability reconciliation catching the discrepancy

- **Revenue-misrecognition risk**: the cashier posts the load as revenue (not liability), overstating revenue and understating liability; mitigated by the system-controlled posting (the cashier can't override the liability-vs-revenue split)
System Touchpoints: - POS / stored-value (links to VS-08 / W5B, W28 gift card liability, POS-013 real-time) — the activation and liability posting
- Stored-value liability GL (links to VS-17 / W28) — the liability account (Dr. Cash, Cr. Gift Card Liability)
- AMLA KYC (links to VS-86 / W2148) — the high-value-cash-purchase trigger
Time Estimate: ~1.5 min/transaction × ~17,500/month = **~440 hours/month Cashier time** (absorbed into the checkout role, not incremental headcount).

steps.activity: Cashier scans the physical card; system prompts for load amount; customer pays; system activates the card (registers the sequential number to the stored-value liability) and prints a receipt; for cash purchases ≥PHP 50K, AMLA KYC applies (W2148)
System posts the sale: cash/card receipt to revenue-bank, load amount to gift-card liability (not revenue — revenue is recognized at redemption per PFRS 15)

fields.Trigger: Customer purchases digital gift card online

Automation Opportunity: - Digital-card issuance and delivery fully automated; fraud-hold auto-routed to the analyst worklist
Controls: - CTL-391 (ensure controlled execution — Gift Card Issuance & Distribution (PA-54.1).)
- operational: Ecommerce Ops monitoring of the fraud-hold queue
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stolen-payment-issuance risk**: a fraudster buys a digital card with a stolen credit card and redeems it before the chargeback lands; mitigated by the fraud-filter hold and the redemption-speed limit on newly-issued digital cards
- **Delivery-failure risk**: the email/SMS doesn't reach the recipient (typo, spam filter), and the customer disputes the charge; mitigated by the delivery-confirmation and the resend mechanism
System Touchpoints: - Ecommerce / stored-value (links to VS-10 / W11 BOPIS, W180 marketplace; VS-08 / W28) — the digital-card issuance and delivery
- Email/SMS gateway (links to VS-10) — the delivery channel
- Fraud filter (links to VS-125 / W266 ecommerce fraud) — the hold-and-review control
Time Estimate: System automated; Ecommerce Ops ~4 hours/week monitoring = **~200 hours/year**.

steps.activity: Customer selects denomination and recipient (self or gift recipient) on ecommerce/app; pays online; system generates a digital card number, emails/SMSes it to the recipient, and posts the liability
For fraudulent-pattern transactions (rapid high-value purchases, stolen-card payment), the fraud filter (links to VS-125) holds the digital-card issuance pending review

fields.Participants: Corporate Sales Mgr, Head of Trade / Account Management, Finance

Automation Opportunity: - Bulk activation via file upload with pre-validation; invoice auto-generated per the corporate terms
Controls: - CTL-391 (ensure controlled execution — Gift Card Issuance & Distribution (PA-54.1).)
- operational: Head of Trade / Account Management sign-off on bulk orders >PHP 500K
Pain Points / Risks: - **Bulk-activation-error risk**: a bulk activation loads the wrong amount or wrong card range, creating a large liability discrepancy; mitigated by the pre-activation validation (test activation on a sample before the full bulk run)

- **Corporate-default risk**: the corporate client is invoiced (not prepaid) and defaults on payment while the cards are already activated; mitigated by the credit-check (W24) and the prepaid-default for new corporate clients
System Touchpoints: - Stored-value / bulk activation (links to VS-08 / W28, VS-16 / W8 AR for invoiced terms) — the bulk activation and billing
- CRM / corporate account (links to VS-11 / W58 corporate account, VS-13 / W24 credit application) — the corporate client record
- AMLA KYC (links to VS-86 / W2148) — the bulk-cash threshold
Time Estimate: ~2 hours/order × ~25 orders/month = **~600 hours/year** Corporate Sales Manager.

steps.activity: Corporate Sales Manager processes the bulk order: denomination, quantity, custom branding if requested, payment terms (often invoiced vs. prepaid); for bulk cash orders ≥ threshold, AMLA KYC applies

System bulk-activates the card range to the stored-value liability on payment receipt; delivers physical (to the corporate client) or digital (to the client's recipient list); invoices per the corporate payment terms

fields.Participants: Marketing Promotions Mgr, VP Marketing, Finance, Finance Manager
fields.Trigger: Marketing launches gift card promotion (e.g., buy PHP 5K get PHP 500 bonus)

Automation Opportunity: - Bonus-load auto-applied at the promo threshold; separate-liability-tranche auto-configured
Controls: - CTL-391 (ensure controlled execution — Gift Card Issuance & Distribution (PA-54.1).)
- operational: promo-spend accuracy; CTL-283 (campaign regulatory compliance — DTI promo-permit review per W833); operational: Finance sign-off on the bonus-liability tranche
Pain Points / Risks: - **Promo-fraud risk**: a fraudster exploits the bonus structure (buy PHP 5K, get PHP 500 bonus, redeem the PHP 5K for cash equivalent, keep the PHP 500); mitigated by the no-cashout-on-bonus term and the fraud-monitoring (W2160)
- **Revenue-misrecognition risk**: the bonus liability is commingled with the paid liability, distorting breakage accounting; mitigated by the separate liability tranche in step 2
System Touchpoints: - Stored-value / promo config (links to VS-08 / W28, VS-58 / coupon, VS-14 / W13 promotions) — the bonus-load configuration
- Marketing/promo (links to VS-14 / W83 campaign) — the promo execution
- DTI permit (links to VS-22 / W868) — the "Per DTI Permit No." requirement on the promo

steps.activity: Marketing designs the promo (bonus structure, eligibility, channel); configures the bonus-load in the stored-value system; promotes across channels; tracks redemption and lift vs. baseline
Finance validates the bonus-load accounting (the bonus is a separate liability tranche with a different breakage/revenue-recognition treatment per PFRS 15)

fields.Trigger: Monthly performance review or new channel activation

Controls: - CTL-391 (ensure controlled execution — Gift Card Issuance & Distribution (PA-54.1).)
- Operational: VP Marketing monthly channel-review sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **Channel-cannibalization risk**: a new channel (app) grows by shifting sales from POS, not by growing the total; mitigated by the total-program view alongside the channel view

- **Channel-cost-blindness risk**: a high-volume channel (corporate bulk) carries hidden servicing cost (custom branding, invoicing) that erodes its net contribution; mitigated by the channel-profitability analysis (W2165)
System Touchpoints: - Analytics/BI (links to VS-27 / W113) — the channel-performance dataset
- Channel platforms (links to VS-08 POS, VS-10 ecommerce, VS-75 app, VS-11 corporate) — the 4 channels
- Stored-value (links to VS-08 / W28) — the channel-tagged liability

steps.activity: Marketing Ops Manager reviews monthly channel performance: sales volume, average denomination, customer segment, channel cost; identifies growth opportunities and underperforming channels

fields.Participants: Legal Compliance Officer, VP Legal & Compliance
fields.Trigger: BSP regulation update or annual review
fields.Volume: BSP stored-value regulations; Consumer Act; AMLA

Automation Opportunity: - AMLA-threshold auto-aggregated per customer/day; expiry disabled on sold gift checks per RA 10962 (loyalty/promo cards carry program terms)
Controls: - CTL-391 (AMLA KYC — links to VS-86); CTL-211 (consumer-protection / stored-value expiry — links to VS-22 / W2682); operational: VP Legal annual compliance sign-off
Pain Points / Risks: - **AMLA-exposure risk**: a structured cash purchase (multiple sub-threshold cards to evade the PHP 50K KYC) goes undetected; mitigated by the aggregation-logic in the KYC trigger (single-customer, single-day aggregation)

- **Expiry-non-compliance risk**: a sold gift check carries an expiry date, violating RA 10962 (no expiry/dormancy fees on gift checks; loyalty/promo program cards are the exempt class); mitigated by the no-expiry setting enforced at the stored-value-system level for sold cards
System Touchpoints: - Compliance / T&Cs (links to VS-22 / W22.1 regulatory, VS-88 / W255 document) — the program T&Cs and disclosures
- AMLA KYC (links to VS-86 / W2143 trigger) — the high-value-cash KYC
- Breakage accounting (links to VS-17 / W28, W2156) — the PFRS 15 treatment
Time Estimate: ~40 hours/year Legal Compliance Officer + ad-hoc = **~50–60 hours/year**.

steps.activity: Legal & Compliance Officer monitors the regulatory framework: BSP stored-value-product rules (disclosure, expiry limits, consumer protection), RA 7394 Consumer Act (clear terms, no deceptive practices), RA 9160 AMLA (KYC on cash purchases ≥PHP 50K — single or aggregated), BIR revenue-recognition (PFRS 15 breakage)

Officer ensures BuildRight's program complies: T&Cs posted, no expiry on sold gift checks per RA 10962 (Gift Check Act of 2017 — valid until issued/used); program terms only on loyalty/promotional gift cards (RA 10962 §5-exempt), AMLA KYC triggered on the threshold, breakage accounting per PFRS 15

Controls: - CTL-391 (ensure controlled execution — Gift Card Issuance & Distribution (PA-54.1).)
- CTL-391 (denomination config integrity); operational: VP Marketing sign-off on denomination changes
Pain Points / Risks: - **Denomination-mismatch risk**: the standard denominations don't match customer intent (e.g., no PHP 1,500 denomination for a typical gift amount), suppressing sales; mitigated by the custom-load option alongside the standard set
- **High-denomination-fraud risk**: the PHP 10K denomination is a fraud target (high value, portable); mitigated by the AMLA KYC on high-value cash purchases (W2143/2148)
System Touchpoints: - Stored-value / denomination config (links to VS-08 / W28, VS-29 / W296) — the standard-denomination master
- Analytics (links to VS-27 / W113) — the denomination-performance dataset
- POS (links to VS-08 / W5B) — the denomination selection at sale

steps.activity: Category Manager reviews denomination performance: which denominations sell best, average load vs. face value, custom-load adoption; adjusts the standard-denomination set and the custom-load limits
